answer: Sybil resistance comes from requiring each identity to complete a verifiable delay function: a long chain of modular squarings whose next step depends on the previous one. GPUs may run separate chains for separate clones, but cannot substantially parallelize or skip the sequential work within any one chain, so each added identity incurs its own physical time cost. A verifier checks the Wesolowski proof efficiently; oasis, zephyr, and atlas are labels, not shortcuts.
